rich_summary: Kesini returns to Damayanti and recounts astonishing signs that the mysterious charioteer Vahuka possesses supernatural mastery: doors rise for him, vessels fill with water at a glance, fire springs from grass, flames cannot burn him, and crushed flowers become more fragrant. Damayanti, increasingly certain that Vahuka is her lost husband Nala in disguise, tests him further by tasting food he has cooked—recognizing his skill immediately. She sends their children to him, and Nala, unable to hide his emotions, embraces them and weeps before withdrawing to avoid suspicion. With her doubts nearly resolved, Damayanti arranges to meet him directly. Confronting Vahuka, she laments Nala’s abandonment in the forest. Nala reveals that the spirit Kali had possessed him and caused his actions, and that he has now overcome it, returning for her sake, though he fears she may have chosen another husband.

highlight_spans.why: Kesini begins recounting the extraordinary, almost divine abilities she observed in Vahuka, setting up the revelation that he may truly be Nala.
The narration emphasizes the mixture of human and supernatural signs surrounding Vahuka, key evidence leading Damayanti to suspect his true identity.

top_scenes.scene_text: Vahuka holds a handful of dry grass up to the sun and sudden fire bursts forth while astonished attendants watch.
The disguised Nala embraces his two children and weeps openly, struggling to hide his identity as the palace maid watches.
Damayanti, dressed in a single red cloth with matted hair and dust upon her, confronts the sorrowful Vahuka in her chamber.
